# Find

Finds the first element of an array for which a lambda gives a truthy result.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Find(items, callback)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to search. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `callback` | function | A lambda of exactly one parameter, which receives the element; the element matches when the lambda's result is truthy. A lambda of any other number of parameters, or a value that is not a lambda, null included, is a runtime error. |

## Returns

Any. The first element that matches. Null when no element matches, or when the element that matches is itself null.

## Remarks

The lambda is called for each element in order, and not for any element after the first match. It is given the elements the array holds when the call starts, so a change the lambda makes to the array does not change which elements it is given.

## Example

`Find([1, 5, 8], x => x > 4)` returns 5.
